To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
machine learning models can be vulnerable to adversarial attack, and that the vulnerability is dependent on the type of attack, the type of data, and the type of machine learning model used.
(1) Machine learning models are highly vulnerable to adversarially generated data.
(1) Machine learning models are highly vulnerable to adverserial attacks in adverserial environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Can we build ML-based detection systems to identify malicious workers in a crowdsourcing system?
the following questions: (1) What are the most practical and effective adversarial attacks against ML models?
the following questions: How can attackers exploit the vulnerabilities in ML detectors to evade them?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ML model is vulnerable to a wide variety of adversarial attacks and the results show that the ML model has a low detection accuracy when faced with adversarial attacks.
our analysis provides a detailed practical look into adversarial attacks on machine learning detectors, and helps defenders in the design and deployment of ML models.
our results indicate the importance of considering adversarial settings in the development and deployment of ML systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to study practical adversarial attacks against ML models in the context crowdsourcing systems.
we show how attackers can evade ML models in the context on crowdsourcing.
the adversarial attacks against ML models in malicious crowdsourcing systems are very powerful and effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ML classifiers are highly vulnerable to adversarially trained attackers.
ML models are highly vulnerable in adversarial environments.
adversarial models must be considered in the design of ML-based detectors.
